articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
articles.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
articles.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.

articles.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
articles.summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

articles.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
articles.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.summary: The British cyber agency says that "building strong foundations has never mattered more" as AI hacking tools rely on exploiting simple security flaws.

articles.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users 'DJ their art'
articles.summary: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control—part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (smart fridges).

articles.title: What are AI chips, and what's so special about Nvidia's?
articles.summary: The commotion around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement, the central role of Nvidia in the U.S.–China AI competition and the U.S. economy's reliance on the AI boom might leave you asking: What's so special about Nvidia's chips?

articles.title: After AI, EU bets on quantum as next big thing
articles.summary: Fearing Europe could lose ground in another technology race, as it lags behind the United States and China on AI, the European Union will unveil plans on Wednesday that it says will make the continent a global quantum computing powerhouse.

articles.summary: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. articles.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
articles.summary: Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen. The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 […]

articles.summary: Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. Suddenly, from behind him, Alice Huang - the Chinese technology executive and suspected spy he […]

articles.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
articles.summary: The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI "in ways that may not be apparent to users." In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times' photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh […]

articles.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
articles.summary: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would "end up on his feet." […]

articles.title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
articles.summary: I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened. Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a "free market" is might […]

articles.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
articles.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.

articles.title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
articles.summary: Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: On-demand bus routing draws on slime mold to rethink public transit
articles.summary: What if catching a bus were as easy as calling an Uber, without the steep fare or the long walk to a stop? NJIT biologist Simon Garnier thinks an unlikely organism could help make that possible—slime mold.

articles.title: Inflatable FaBrick enables soft robots to contract, bend and twist
articles.summary: Soft robots that contract, bend, twist, rotate or stiffen can be built from the same pneumatically actuated fabric with easily accessible tools, according to a University of Michigan Engineering study. The fabric, embedded with a grid of inflatable pouches, earned the name FaBrick as the design drew inspiration from modular building blocks like LEGO bricks.

articles.title: Finding the catalyst sweet spot for turning CO₂ into methane
articles.summary: Capturing carbon dioxide is only one part of the climate challenge. Another question is what to do with the captured CO₂. One promising route is to convert CO₂ into useful fuels and chemicals, especially when the process can be paired with renewable hydrogen.

articles.title: Researchers use data from 130 wells worldwide to speed up drilling-fluid solids checks
articles.summary: As the world faces ongoing pressure to secure reliable energy supplies while controlling costs and improving operational efficiency, even small delays in drilling operations can have significant consequences. For oil, gas and geothermal drilling, one of the routine but important checks is determining how much solid material is present in the drilling fluid.

articles.title: Fake gifts, real losses as AI ads proliferate
articles.summary: Online shoppers endlessly scrolling through gift suggestions this holiday season risk being duped by a blizzard of AI-generated scams touting nonexistent products.

articles.title: An unclassified CIA system was breached in a cyberattack
articles.summary: An unclassified CIA system was breached in a cyberattack, according to a person familiar with the incident who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity.

articles.title: Georgia Waffle House cuts cooling energy use by 40% with new salt-based AC system
articles.summary: In July 2025, a team of technicians walked into a Waffle House in Macon, Georgia. That month, peak temperatures hovered around 92 degrees Fahrenheit (33 degrees Celsius). In the restaurant's kitchen, where cooks fried patty melts, hash browns and waffles on an oil-slick grill, temperatures could feel just as hot, if not hotter.
